problem:
Given that ${\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=4$ and ${\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-6,$ 
then what is ${\int }_{2}^{9}(3-2f(x))\,\text{d}x?$

${\int }_{2}^{9}(3-2f(x))\,\text{d}x=$ 
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{5}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,=\,{\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
4+(-6)\,=\,{\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-2.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{9}(3-2f(x))\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{2}^{9}1\,\text{d}x\,-\,2{\int }_{2}^{9}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\cdot x{|}_{2}^{9}\,-\,2(-2) \\  & =3(9-2)+4 \\  & =21+4 \\  & =25\end{aligned}
$$
